rows.rationale: Three-way match is exact: PO, receipt (GR-7701) and invoice all show 200 EACH at $4.20 (clauses 1, 3, 4). Recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate is $63.00, identical to the supplier figure (clause 5). No non-PO lines, no prior invoices or open credit memos, so the $903.00 gross stands and falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The only exception was a unit-of-measure difference: the supplier billed 480 EACH @ $2.00 where the PO was raised as 40 CASE @ $24.00 (pack size 12). Normalised under clause 2 the quantity (40 CASE, matching GR-7702) and unit price match exactly, so it is a clean 3-way match, not a defect. Tax at the vendor's 7.5% recomputes to $72.00, identical to the invoice (clause 5). No credit memos; $1,032.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The $1.10/unit price increase (62.00 -> 63.10) is 1.77%, inside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $1.24 and $50.00), so it is not a defect. GOODS three-way match is complete: GR-7703 confirms 100 EACH received against 100 ordered and 100 invoiced (clause 1, clause 4). Recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate equals the invoiced $473.25 exactly (clause 5), no credit memos are open (clause 9), and $6,783.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $154.00/EACH vs PO $145.00/EACH (+6.21%, $9.00) against an allowance of $2.90 (lower of 2% and $50.00), with no authorisation from a listed buyer
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (80 EACH ordered, received, invoiced) and tax recomputes to $924.00 exactly, so the only issue is price. The 6.2% increase exceeds the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $2.90 and $50.00). The only supporting evidence is the supplier's own price notice from its billing department; it is not from or countersigned by an authorised buyer (Dele Fashanu or Priya Raman), so clause 3.1 does not cure it. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation: hold for buyer action at $0.00.

The invoiced unit price of $93.28 is exactly 6% above the PO price of $88.00, outside the 2% / $50 tolerance (clause 3), but it is cured under clause 3.1: authorised buyer Dele Fashanu (listed in vendor.json) approved up to 6% on PO-4405, conduit line only, in writing. Receipt GR-7705 confirms all 60 EACH delivered (clause 4) and tax of $419.76 matches the recomputed 7.5% exactly (clause 5). No defects, no credit memos; $6,016.56 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 100 EACH invoiced but only 60 EACH received (40 on backorder) — clause 4 under-delivery
rows.rationale: Goods PO with a receipt for only 60 of 100 EACH (balance on backorder), so under clause 4 the payable is calculated on the received quantity: 60 x $9.50 = $570.00. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3, no variance). Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% on the corrected net gives $42.75, so gross $612.75; the supplier's $71.25 simply follows the over-invoiced quantity and is not a separate defect. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; $612.75 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Suspected duplicate: prior paid invoice NW-9912 matches on vendor, PO-4407, gross $3,225.00 and falls 19 days apart with no distinguishing service period
rows.rationale: All five clause 8 duplicate conditions are met against prior PAID invoice NW-9912 in vendor.json: same vendor after suffix normalisation (Nordwind Supply Co. / Nordwind Supply Company LLC), same PO-4407, identical $3,225.00 gross, 19 days apart, and both invoices carry a null service_period so clause 8.1 does not apply. Price, quantity (25 EACH ordered, received and invoiced) and tax (7.5% = $225.00 exactly) are otherwise clean, so the duplicate is the sole defect and no clause 11 escalation is triggered. Payable is $0.00 per clause 12, approver AP_CLERK per clause 10.

March 2026 retainer bills the same amount as the paid February invoice, but the service periods are distinct and non-overlapping, so it is a legitimate recurring charge, not a duplicate (clause 8.1). SERVICES PO needs only 2-way match, so the absent goods receipt is not a defect (clause 1). Price matches the blanket PO exactly (clause 3) and tax recomputes to $360.00 at 7.5% (clause 5). No open credit memos; $5,160.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9-10).

Line 1 matches PO and receipt exactly on quantity (150 EACH) and unit price ($18.00), within tolerance (clause 3). The $380.00 expedited freight line is a permitted non-PO pass-through: contract clause 6.2 allows actual expedited carrier charges up to $500.00, the receipt note confirms production requested overnight delivery, and the amount is under the ceiling and the clause 6 $500 limit, so it is not a defect. Recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate is $231.00, matching the invoice (clause 5). No credit memos; net payable $3,311.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Tax overcharge: supplier billed $744.00 tax (12%) versus $465.00 at the vendor's 7.5% rate — $279.00 discrepancy beyond the $0.02 rounding allowance (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Price and quantity match the PO and receipt exactly (clauses 3, 4), so the only defect is tax: the supplier applied 12% instead of the vendor's registered 7.5% rate, overcharging $279.00 (clause 5). Short-pay the corrected total of $6,665.00 ($6,200.00 net + $465.00 tax). Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; $6,665.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Contract clause 4.2 fixes EUR 1.00 = USD 1.10 for invoices dated in Q1 2026, so the USD invoicing is normalisation, not a defect (policy clause 7). The PO price of EUR 210.00/EACH converts to exactly USD 231.00, matching the invoiced unit price (clause 3), receipt GR-7711 confirms 40 of 40 EACH delivered (clauses 1 and 4), and recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% is exactly USD 693.00 (clause 5). No credit memos; net payable USD 9,933.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Over-delivery beyond 5%: PO ordered 100 EACH, receipt GR-7712 shows 118 EACH received and invoiced (18.0% over, tolerance 5%)
rows.rationale: Unit price matches the PO exactly and tax recomputes to the cent, so the only issue is quantity: the receipt confirms 118 EACH against a PO of 100 EACH, an 18% over-delivery well beyond the 5% band in clause 4, making this a quantity defect requiring receiving action. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; HOLD sets payable to 0.00 per clause 12, with approver read from that net figure under clause 10.

PO-4413 is a SERVICES PO, so the absent goods receipt is expected and not a defect (clause 1). Price matches the PO exactly (clause 3), tax recomputes to $562.50 at the vendor's 7.5% rate with zero delta (clause 5), no non-PO lines, no prior invoices to test for duplication (clause 8) and no open credit memos. Net payable $8,062.50 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 1050 CASE received against 1200 CASE invoiced (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed 3,240.00 (9%) against the 7.5% vendor rate; correct tax on the corrected net is 2,362.50 (clause 5)
rows.rationale: UOM normalises cleanly (30,000 EACH at $1.20 = 1,200 CASE at $30.00, matching the PO exactly), so price is within tolerance and the conversion is not a defect (clauses 2, 3). Two defects remain: the receipt shows only 1,050 of 1,200 cases delivered, so the line short-pays to $31,500.00 (clause 4), and the supplier applied 9% tax instead of the vendor's 7.5%, giving correct tax of $2,362.50 and gross $33,862.50 (clause 5). Netting the open credit memo CM-2026-014 of $1,500.00 leaves $32,362.50 (clause 9). Two defects plus a payable above $25,000.00 force escalation to the Controller (clauses 10, 11).

defects: Quantity shortfall on line 4: 25 EACH invoiced, 20 EACH received (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed 609.84 (9.0% of net) vs 7.5% vendor rate; correct tax on corrected net is 463.20, a 146.64 overcharge (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Line 2 reconciles exactly once the CASE->EACH pack size of 12 is applied (40 CASE @ $24.60 = 480 EACH @ $2.05), and line 3's $45.80 vs $45.00 is inside the lower-of-2%/$50 band ($0.90) — neither is a defect (clauses 2, 3). Two defects remain: line 4 was part-shipped (20 of 25 received), so it pays on the receipt at $2,400.00 (clause 4), and the supplier applied a 9.0% tax rate instead of the vendor's 7.5% (clause 5). Corrected net $6,176.00 + tax $463.20 = $6,639.20; two defects force ESCALATE_HUMAN under clause 11 with this recommended payable, approval band AP_CLERK (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $4,075.00/EACH vs PO $4,000.00/EACH, a $75.00 per-unit variance against the $50.00 allowance
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (2 EACH ordered, received and invoiced) and tax recomputes to $611.25 exactly at the vendor's 7.5% rate, so the only issue is price. The invoiced unit price exceeds the PO price by $75.00, above the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $80.00 and the $50.00 cap = $50.00), and the case file contains no buyer authorisation referencing PO-4416, so clause 3.1 does not cure it. One defect only, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered; hold for buyer action at $0.00.

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $19.60/EACH vs PO $18.00/EACH (8.89%, allowance $0.36) with no authorisation from a listed buyer (clauses 3, 3.1)
rows.rationale: The $1.60/EACH copper surcharge takes the unit price 8.89% above the PO price, far outside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% / $50 = $0.36). The only approval referencing PO-4417 is from Femi Okonkwo, a warehouse supervisor who is not in vendor.json authorised_buyers, so clause 3.1 does not cure it; Dele Fashanu's approval is expressly limited to PO-4405. Quantities match the receipt and tax recomputes exactly, so this is the single defect: hold for buyer action per clauses 11.1 and 12.

defects: Unauthorised non-PO surcharge: $640.00 delivery and handling line exceeds the $500.00 clause 6 limit
rows.rationale: Line 1 matches the PO and receipt exactly (6 EACH @ $410.00, within tolerance, no quantity variance). Line 2 is a non-PO delivery and handling charge of $640.00: contract clause 6.2 permits passing through oversize transport cost, but clause 6 of the policy also caps such charges at $500.00, and clause 6.3 of the contract expressly preserves internal approval limits. That single unauthorised-surcharge defect gives HOLD_PRICE_VARIANCE with a $0.00 payable (clauses 6, 11.1, 12); the tax gap is purely a consequence of the disallowed freight line, not an independent discrepancy.

defects: Tax undercharged: supplier billed $65.00 vs recomputed $97.50 at the vendor's 7.5% rate (clause 5) — $32.50 tax-compliance exposure
rows.rationale: Price and quantity match the PO and receipt exactly (clauses 3, 4), and the GOODS PO has its goods receipt (clause 1). The only defect is tax: the supplier applied 5% instead of the vendor's 7.5% rate, so tax is $97.50 not $65.00. Clause 5 requires paying the recomputed higher total of $1,397.50 while flagging the undercharge; a single defect does not trigger clause 11 escalation. No credit memos to net (clause 9); AP_CLERK per clause 10.

Supplier shipped a full carton: 206 EACH received against 200 ordered, a 3.0% over-delivery within the 5% tolerance, so the received/invoiced quantity is payable and is not a defect (clause 4). Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3), and the supplier's tax of $125.15 is $0.01 from the recomputed $125.14 at the 7.5% vendor rate, i.e. rounding only (clause 5). No credit memos; net payable $1,793.75 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9-10).

Price, quantity (12 EACH ordered, received and invoiced) and 7.5% tax all reconcile exactly against the PO and goods receipt, so the three-way match is clean with no defects (clauses 1, 3, 4, 5). The open $2,000.00 credit memo CM-2026-021 nets against the $1,522.20 gross under clause 9, flooring the payable at $0.00; netting is not a defect (clause 11.1). Approval sits with AP_CLERK per clause 10.

The prior invoice HL-3301 shares the PO and gross amount, but it carries a distinct service period (2026-02-01/2026-02-28) versus this invoice's 2026-02-15/2026-03-14, and the billed name does not normalise to the same vendor string, so clause 8's five conditions are not all met — this is a legitimate recurring charge under clause 8.1. Price matches the PO line exactly, tax recomputes to $300.00 at the 7.5% vendor rate (clause 5), no receipt is expected on a SERVICES PO (clause 1), and no open credit memos exist. Net payable $4,300.00 sits in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The $242.00/EACH invoiced price exceeds the PO's $220.00 by $22.00, outside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $4.40 and $50.00), but it is cured under clause 3.1: authorised buyer Priya Raman (vendor.json authorised_buyers) authorised in writing a $250.00 per-enclosure ceiling specifically for PO-4423, which covers $242.00. Receipt GR-7723 matches 15 EACH ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and tax of $272.25 equals 7.5% of the $3,630.00 net exactly (clause 5). No defects; $3,902.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 60 EACH invoiced, only 52 EACH received (8 kits damaged and refused at the dock) — clause 4 under-delivery
rows.rationale: Goods receipt GR-7724 shows 52 of 60 EACH accepted (8 refused as damaged), so under clause 4 the quantity dispute resolves in favour of the receipt: 52 × $320.00 = $16,640.00 net. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3). Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% on the corrected net is $1,248.00, giving a corrected gross of $17,888.00 (clause 5 — the supplier's $1,440.00 simply reflects the over-invoiced quantity, not a separate tax error). Single defect, no credit memos, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered; $17,888.00 falls in the AP_MANAGER band (clause 10).
